headline: Yesterday's bond-vol relief was a head fake: today real yields stopped hitting bonds and started liquidating collateral — gold -3.5%, miners -5%, IG credit at a 52-week low, VIX bid.
summary: The relief lasted exactly one session. The credit & vol composite collapsed from +46 to +21 and risk regime slipped to -13 from -10, while rates stayed pinned at -76. TLT fell 1.1% to 78.49, an outright 52-week low; LQD fell 0.7% and sits at the 0th percentile of the past year, -3.3% on the month (z=-1.32); IEF is also at the 0th percentile with z=-1.56. HYG finally cracked, -0.4% with z=-1.46 and a rolling_over trend, even though HYG/IEF is still +1.1% on the month at the 96th percentile. VIX rose 6.8% to 15.88 and the VIX/VIX3M term structure lifted 5.8% with acceleration z=1.42 — the first time the vol complex has confirmed the rates complex in a month. With the 30-year at 5.49% (100th percentile), the 10-year real yield at 2.83% (+49bp in a month, z=1.94) and the 30-year mortgage at 7.03%, the debate has moved from how many cuts to whether the next move is a hike.

The clearing trade was precious metals, and it was violent. Gold fell 3.5% to 4,168 with an acceleration z of -3.03 and is now -8.0% on the month, 8.6% below its 200-day and at the 21st percentile. Silver -4.2%, platinum -1.4% (-5.3% on the month), GDX -4.8% with acceleration z=-3.26, GDXJ -5.0%, NEM -4.1% with acceleration z=-3.22, and GDX/gold accelerating at -3.0. Yesterday's stabilization in silver and platinum was noise, not a base. This is a real-yield-plus-dollar event: DXY +0.2% to 101.15, turning up with acceleration 0.97, USDCHF at a 52-week high, EURUSD at the 3rd percentile, and USDMXN +0.8% to 17.88 (+5.4% on the month, z=2.1, acceleration 2.01). The EM FX squeeze is the one stress that has accelerated four sessions running.

Critically, this is not a growth scare, and that dictates what you short. Copper/gold rose another 2.8% today, +9.9% on the month at the 99th percentile; oil/gold +3.7% (+20.5% on the month); XLI/XLU sits at a 52-week high at the 98.5th percentile; growth pulse holds at +17. WTI is 92.46, +10.9% on the month, with crude bid again on failed talks over a key shipping chokepoint even as RBOB fell 6.8% (-9.4% on the month) and Brent printed -6.3%. That crude-versus-product split, plus wheat -10.4% on the month and breakevens frozen at 2.34% (5y +3bp in a month), pushed the inflation composite up to -34 from -38. So the pain is concentrated in duration, leverage and hard-asset momentum — not cyclicals broadly.

Inside equities, leadership fractured but did not fail. SPX -0.6%, NDX -0.9%. The month's winners took the hit: META -4.0% after a +24.9% month (z=1.98), AMD -4.0% while still 64% above its 200-day, TSLA -3.5%, MU -2.6%, SOXX -2.2%, BA -6.0%, ORCL -2.5% and now -52.3% year-on-year at the 10th percentile. But NVDA +2.1%, ASML +2.2%, TSM +0.6% and XBI +1.4% — dispersion, not de-risking. Breadth ratios ticked up microscopically (RSP/SPY +0.1%, IWM/SPY +0.2%, XRT/SPY +0.9%) off z-scores of -2.07, -1.30 and -0.82; that is a dead-cat tick, not repair. The honest tell is financials: XLF -6.2% on the month (z=-1.48), BX -19.3% (z=-1.99), GS -10.8%, IAI -8.1%, KIE -6.6%. The leverage complex is derating while SPY still sits 7.1% above its 200-day at the 94th percentile. That gap is the trade.

good.text: The growth signal did not blink: copper/gold +2.8% today and +9.9% on the month at the 99th percentile, oil/gold +3.7%, XLI/XLU at a 52-week high, growth pulse +17. The selloff is a rates event, not a demand event.

Inflation expectations refuse to follow crude: 5-year breakevens 2.34% (+3bp in a month, z=0.10), 10-year 2.34%, RBOB -6.8% today and -9.4% on the month, wheat -10.4%. Inflation composite improved to -34 from -38.
AI/semi leadership is dispersing, not breaking: NVDA +2.1%, ASML +2.2%, TSM +0.6%, SMH/SPY z=1.11 and +8.7% on the month, SOXX +10.2% on the month, Taiwan's EWT at the 97th percentile.
Crypto is quietly the best-behaving risk asset: BTC +7.2%, ETH +9.5%, SOL +13.2% and MSTR +25.2% on the month, all turning_up, with ETH/BTC +2.1% — no funding stress despite a firmer dollar.
Front-end relief is real even if the long end won't play: 2-year -6bp to 4.81%, 5-year -5bp to 4.98%, MOVE -8.2% to 96, 3m10y +12bp on the month.
Health care is the one defensive that works on fundamentals: XLV +0.3% and rs +3.0% over 3m, IBB +0.6% (+50.0% y/y), XBI +1.4%, LLY +0.3% with rs turning up.

bad.text: The credit-vol cushion that offset rates all month broke: composite 46 to 21 in one day. HYG -0.4% (z=-1.46, rolling over), LQD -0.7% at the 0th percentile, IEF at the 0th percentile, TLT -1.1% to a 52-week low.
Precious metals liquidation is accelerating, not stabilizing: gold -3.5% (acc z=-3.03), silver -4.2%, GDX -4.8% (acc z=-3.26), GDXJ -5.0%, NEM -4.1% (acc z=-3.22), GDX/gold acc z=-3.0.

The long end is still the problem: 30-year 5.49% at the 100th percentile, 10-year real yield 2.83% (+49bp on the month), 30-year mortgage 7.03% at a 52-week high, 3-month bill 4.24% with acceleration z=1.84.
Vol is turning up from the floor: VIX +6.8% to 15.88 (14th percentile), VIX/VIX3M +5.8% with acceleration 1.42, SKEW turning up. Cheap protection is starting to bid — the worst time to be short it.

The dollar squeeze is broadening: DXY turning up with acceleration 0.97, USDCHF at a 52-week high (+3.5% on the month), USDMXN z=2.1/acc 2.01, EURUSD at the 3rd percentile, CEW -0.4% and AUDJPY -3.6% on the month.
Leverage and hard-asset thematics are being repriced together: BX -19.3% and XLF -6.2% on the month, GS -10.8%, IAI -8.1%; REMX -16.4%, NLR -11.6% (acc -2.33), XME -10.9% (acc -2.29), TAN -10.9%.

trades.name: Buy index vol before the vol complex catches rates
trades.line: VIX 15.9 at 14th pctile while IG at 52wk low — buy cheap vol
trades.expr: Buy SPX Nov 7,300/6,900 put spreads (~5-10% OTM) funded partly by selling 8,100 calls; alternatively VIX Nov 20/30 call spreads.
trades.thesis: Rates composite -76 against a credit & vol composite that just fell from +46 to +21 is the board's biggest unreconciled spread, and it is closing from the wrong side. With SPY 7.1% above its 200-day at the 94th percentile and VIX at 15.88 (13.7th percentile), convexity is priced for calm that the bond market no longer supports.
trades.trigger: VIX +6.8% and VIX/VIX3M +5.8% with acceleration z=1.42 on a day SPX fell only 0.6%; HYG turned to rolling_over with z=-1.46 and LQD hit the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.
trades.stop: VIX back below 14 with VIX/VIX3M under 0.85 and HYG/IEF making new highs — that means credit absorbed the real-yield shock and vol is a fade again.
trades.target: VIX 24-26 / 4-5% SPX drawdown; monetize put spread at 2.5-3x premium.

trades.name: Short the US consumer at a 7% mortgage
trades.line: Short XLY: mortgage 7.03%, HD and MCD at 52-week lows
trades.expr: Short XLY outright or buy Dec 105 puts; size a portion in HD and MCD single-name puts. Cleaner as XLY vs XLP pair if you want beta out.
trades.thesis: The rate shock transmits to the household through mortgages and revolving credit, and the tape already knows it: XLY -6.5% on the month in a down trend with acceleration -1.23, XLY/XLP -3.5% at the 13th percentile, HD -11.2% and MCD -11.0% both at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, UBER -13.2%, NKE at the 3rd percentile. Falling gasoline is the bull case and it hasn't helped for five weeks.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage at 7.03%, a 52-week high, with homebuilders confirming: XHB -6.1% and ITB -6.7% on the month, XHB/SPY at the 4th percentile; retail/S&P at the 4th percentile.
trades.stop: XLY/XLP reclaiming 1.38 alongside a 10-year real yield back under 2.60% — the consumer gets a rate reprieve and this short becomes a squeeze.

trades.name: Floating rate over long-duration IG
trades.line: Long BKLN vs short LQD: floating over long-duration IG
trades.expr: Long BKLN, short LQD dollar-for-dollar (or short LQD vs long 2y Treasury futures if you want spread-only).
trades.thesis: IG index duration is the purest loser of a term-premium repricing with no growth offset. LQD is -3.3% on the month at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks while loans are +0.4% on the month and +2.6% over 3 months at the 92nd percentile, because coupons reset with a 4.24% bill and defaults aren't the story yet.
trades.trigger: LQD -0.7% and TLT -1.1% to a fresh 52-week low today with the 30-year at 5.49% (100th percentile); BKLN only -0.2% and still in an up trend.
trades.stop: Loan prices breaking down with HYG/IEF turning lower (below 0.855) — that flips the trade from a duration call into a credit call, which BKLN loses.
trades.target: Another 350-450bp of relative performance over the quarter.

trades.name: Copper over gold, expressed in the miners
trades.line: Copper over gold: long FCX vs short NEM, CU/AU 99th pctile
trades.expr: Long FCX, short NEM, beta-balanced roughly 1:1 notional; add short GDX vs long COPX as the ETF version.
trades.thesis: The same real-yield impulse that is killing bullion supports the industrial metal, because growth is not the problem: copper/gold is at the 99th percentile, +9.9% on the month with acceleration 1.69, while gold is 8.6% below its 200-day. Gold's monetary bid unwinds at 2.83% real yields; copper's physical bid doesn't.
trades.trigger: Today: NEM -4.1% with acceleration z=-3.22 and GDX -4.8% (acc -3.26) versus FCX only -0.3% and copper holding 6.64 at the 92nd percentile; copper/gold +2.8% in a session.
trades.stop: Copper breaking below 6.30 (200-day) or gold reclaiming 4,450 with GDX/gold turning up — a macro reflation-to-fear flip invalidates the leg order.

trades.name: Stay long the EM FX squeeze in the peso
trades.line: Long USD/MXN: z=2.1, acc 2.0, EM FX squeeze accelerating
trades.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month forwards; alternatively buy USD/MXN 18.50 calls. Equity overlay: short EWW.
trades.thesis: The peso is the most crowded carry long into a rising-real-yield dollar. When the funding currency's real yield rises 49bp in a month, high-carry EM is where the pain lands first, and Mexico's local equity tape is already confirming with EWW -5.3% on the month.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +0.8% today to 17.878, +5.4% on the month with z=2.10 and acceleration 2.01 — the highest acceleration on the FX board; USDCHF at a 52-week high and CEW -1.1% on the month even as DXY only rose 1.4%.
trades.stop: USDMXN back under 17.35 with CEW making new highs — carry re-establishes and the squeeze is over.

trades.name: Short the leverage complex, not the banks' credit
trades.line: Short XLF: leverage complex derating, BX -19% on the month
trades.expr: Buy XLF Dec 52 puts or short XLF; concentrate single-name shorts in BX and GS, avoid shorting KRE outright (deposit beta is already priced).
trades.thesis: Financials were supposed to be the bear-steepener winner; they are the loser because marks, not margins, drive this cycle. XLF is -6.2% on the month (z=-1.48) with relative strength rolling over, while alternative managers and brokers — the entities carrying the duration and private marks — lead lower: BX -19.3% on the month (z=-1.99, acc -1.86), GS -10.8%, IAI -8.1%, KIE -6.6%.
trades.trigger: Today XLF -0.9%, JPM -1.6%, GS -1.9%, BX -2.9%, IAI -1.1% on a 0.6% S&P day, with MOVE still 38.2% higher on the month (z=2.07) and LQD at a 52-week low.
trades.stop: MOVE back under 80 with XLF reclaiming 56.50 and KRE/SPY turning up — a genuine bond-vol collapse rebuilds the sector.

trades.name: Semis dispersion: quality compute vs the extended tail
trades.line: Long NVDA+TSM vs short AMD, 64% above its 200-day
trades.expr: Long a 50/50 NVDA-TSM basket, short AMD, equal notional; or sell AMD Nov upside calls against long SMH.
trades.thesis: Semi leadership is intact but the beta has run too far ahead of the cash flows. AMD is +182.6% YTD and 64.1% above its 200-day with z=1.46; NVDA is 15.1% above its 200-day and made up ground today. When rates compress multiples, the highest-duration equity in the group gives back the most while the earners hold.
trades.trigger: NVDA +2.1% and ASML +2.2% against AMD -4.0% and MU -2.6% on the same day; SOXX -2.2% while SMH/SPY still carries z=1.11.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY breaking under 0.755 (the whole complex de-rates and the long leg loses too) or AMD making new highs above 640 on capacity news.
